about: Daily YouTube recipe pool for MondoTV '98. The updater reads each channel's public RSS feed at youtube.com/feeds/videos.xml. When that feed does not answer, it reads the public channel page and the video description instead, and a failed run keeps the previous file. The page picks today's show from the viewer's calendar date, so the featured video changes every day between updates. Descriptions are parsed for an ingredients list and numbered steps when the chef included them. Not a replacement for the chef's own written recipe.

videos.title: I Made Lasagna The Wrong Way, Im NOT Going Back!
ingredients: 225g (8 oz) hot Italian pork sausage, casings removed
steps: Preheat oven to 400°F/205C. Break the noodles into roughly 2-inch pieces by Grate onions, mince garlic, chop basil.
Heat Dutch oven over medium-high with a squiggle of olive oil. Add the ground beef and sausage and brown, breaking the meat down until fully cooked and about the size of lentils, around 8 minutes
Stir in the onion, garlic and pinch of salt. Cook 3-5 min until the onion is softened
Add tomato paste. Cook, stirring constantly, until the tomato paste darkens to a rusty brick red.
Add the crushed tomatoes, water, chili flake, oregano, BTB and sugar. scrap up any browned bits from the bottom. Bring to simmer, cover partially and cook over low heat 3 to 5 minutes.
Mix the ricotta, Parmesan, salt, black pepper and egg until smooth.
Of heat, taste and adjust with pinch of salt and/or sugar if needed. Stir in basil

Scatter ⅓ of the noodles over the sauce in an even layer and press them down until fully submerged. Repeat two more times pressing each layer beneath the sauce before adding the next. On the final layer, push sauce up and over any exposed noodles.
Spoon the ricotta mixture over the top in 12 to 15 evenly spaced dollops
Top with the mozzarella and Parm
Wipe any sauce off the inside rim of the pot with a damp towel
Cover and bake at 400°F/205C for 15 minutes.
Increase oven temp to 450°F/230C, remove lid and bake for 15 to 20 minutes, until the cheese is deeply browned in spots, edges are bubbling and a knife slides through the noodles with no resistance.
Rest 20 minutes
Homemade Fresh Ricotta:
½ gallon/2000g whole milk
200g or 3/4c + 2 T heavy cream
15g or 2 1/4t salt
100g or 1/3c + 1T white distilled vinegar
Place 4 layers of cheesecloth in a colander with bowl underneath (i use a salad spinner with basket).

videos.title: The FASTER, Better Way to Make Chicken Pot Pie
ingredients: 60 leek, white and light green only, small dice
steps: Dice 220g butter into ½ inch cubes and freeze
Preheat the oven to 425°F. Season chicken with salt. Roast on a rack set in a sheet tray for 20 to 25 minutes to about 175°F.
While the chicken roasts, dice onion, celery, carrot, leek and fennel. Mince garlic and keep it separate.
Heat about neutral oil in a 12 inch cast iron over medium heat. Sweat the veg with a strong pinch of salt for 6 to 8 minutes without browning. Add garlic, cook 2 more mins.
Stir in 75g butter until melted, then add 75g flour and poultry seasoning. Cook, stirring for 1 minute
Deglaze with white wine and stir for 1 to 2 minutes.
Add stock and Better Than Bouillon while stirring. Bring to a simmer, then drop to medium low and cook 3 to 4 minutes while scraping the bottom and corners.
Rest the chicken 5 minutes and drop the oven to 400°F. Shred the chicken then run a knife through
Off heat, stir in chicken, cream and peas. Taste and adjust salt. Let cool while you make the biscuits.
Pulse 275g flour, sugar, baking soda, baking powder and salt in a food processor. Add the 220g frozen butter and pulse in short bursts about 20 times until it's in lentil sized pieces.
Transfer to a bowl, add buttermilk and stir into a shaggy dough.
Drop about 15-16 equal portions, starting around the outside edge and working in.
Set the skillet on a sheet tray and bake at 400°F for 25 to 30 minutes until deeply golden brown.
Rest 10 minutes before serving.

steps: Bring milk, stock, and salt to boil while stirring. Lower heat to med-low. whisk in grits. bring back to a simmer while whisking, til thickened. Cover and cook over low for 90 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes and scraping the bottom well after 1 hour. Add water if they get too thick
Cut shrimp in half lengthwise. season with salt and pepper. Refrigerate.
Dice celery, onion, pepper, and bacon. Mince garlic. Grate cheddar and Parmesan.

With about 40–45 minutes left on the grits, heat dutch oven over medium and cook bacon in splash of oil and water for about 10 minutes until rendered and browned but still flexible. Add another splash water if the pot gets too dark. Move bacon to a bowl.
Add celery, onion, pepper, and pinch of salt. Cook over medium-high 10–12 min until tender and browned.
Add garlic and cook 2 minutes. Deglaze with a splash of water. Add tomato paste and butter. Cook 1-2 minutes
Reduce heat to medium, stir in flour, paprika, cayenne. Whisk in chicken stock and Better Than Bouillon. Simmer 5 minutes until slightly thickened. Return bacon to sauce.
Add the seasoned shrimp to sauce. Cook over medium-low, 3 minutes, until opaque. Taste for seasoning.
When grits are tender, stir in butter, cheddar, parm. Add a splash of stock if needed.
Spoon the grits into bowls and top with the shrimp and sauce. Garnish with minced chives and squeeze of lemon juice.

steps: Bring water to a boil

Add mix-ins, about half the dressing, and grated Parmesan to the cooled pasta. Fold together gently

steps: Slice the filet crosswise into 2 medallions. Pound to even 3/4-inch thickness and season with salt and pepper. rest on plate.

Preheat stainless-steel skillet over medium high to high. Add 3 tablespoons oil. When lightly smoking, pat the steaks VERY dry, add them to pan, and weigh with a heavy sauce pan or burger press. Sear 90 to 120 seconds, flip, sear another 90 seconds while pressing.
Transfer the medium-rare steaks to a plate and reserve the juices.
Carefully wipe out the skillet with damp paper towel. Add 2 tbsp more oil, mushrooms, and pinch of salt. Cook over medium for 5 to 7 minutes, til browned and cooked down.
Add shallot, garlic, and pinch of salt. Reduce the heat to medium/medium low and cook for about 2-3 minutes, until soft and translucent.

Have a lid for the pan closeby. Turn off heat, remove pan from the burner then add cognac. Return pan to burner carefully then relight the burner, and keep your face back. Let the flame die out or cover pan for 20 seconds with lid to smother it. Remove lid and continue cooking uncovered until nearly dry.
Add beef stock, Dijon, cream, and Worcestershire. Boil over medium-high for about 2 minutes stirring frequently, until a spatula dragged through the sauce leaves a lazy trail.
Lower heat to low and whisk in butter. Remove from heat, stir in parsley and thyme.
Taste and adjust the salt. Add the steaks and any resting juices, baste for 20 to 30 seconds, just long enough to rewarm. Serve immediately.

ingredients: As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases*
steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil
Cut chicken thighs into quarters, then into 1/4" slices. Toss with salt, set aside.
Pour boiling water over noodles. Agitate, cut in half. Soak 15 min.
While the noodles soak, prep the aromatics, chop the gai lan, and make the wok sauce by combining oyster sauce, brown sugar, water/stock, fish sauce, soy sauce.
Drain noodles and rinse with cold water
Heat a wok over high. Add half of the oil, gai lan, and a pinch salt. Leave undisturbed for 30 seconds, then stir-fry for 2-3 minutes, until deeply green and about 80% cooked. Transfer to bowl.
Wipe wok with damp paper towel. Return to heat. Add the remaining oil and chicken. Leave undisturbed, 30 to 60 seconds until the edges brown, then stir-fry 2 minutes, until 85% cooked.
Add the garlic, shallot, Thai chiles. Stir fry 2 to 3 minutes until wilted and beginning to color
Return the cooked gai lan to wok. Toss it with chicken. Add noodles. Pour sauce around the hot edges of wok. Reduce 30 to 45 seconds without stirring, then combine until the sauce clings
Off heat add scallion and basil. Stir until the noodles break into 2-3-in lengths. Plate and garnish with additional basil and scallion

steps: Combine the onions, 8g salt, butter, and 25g water in a Dutch oven. Cover and cook over medium heat, stirring every 5 minutes, until dramatically softened and collapsed, about 10 -15 minutes.

Combine stock, worch, BTB, and 5g salt. Whisk in gelatin until dissolved, bring to simmer then reduce 40–50% or for about 10 minutes. Adjust salt.
Combine horseradish sauce ingredients.
Heat the oven to 400°F (205°C), portion and split the rolls, and bring the jus to a boil before lowering it to a gentle simmer.
Toast rolls at 400°F (205°C) for 5 minutes. Add 2 provolone slices to each bottom half and toast open-faced for 3–4 minutes, until the cheese is melted and bubbly
Heat jus to about 135°F (57°C) and move the beef through it for 20–30 seconds. Ribbon on beef, add warm onions and horseradish sauce in thin layers, close, and serve immediately with very hot jus.
